summary: Unbalanced egress path causing high TTFB for dedicated customer in APAC
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (NimbleHealth, dedicated) reports intermittent high time-to-first-byte (TTFB) for inference requests originating from APAC (ap-southeast-1). Symptoms appear as 500–1200ms additional TTFB on many requests; overall completion latency not always elevated because responses stream after initial delay.

Impact:
- Production traffic for NimbleHealth sees increased p50/p95 TTFB and degraded UX for chat product.
- Affects critical inference endpoints pinned to dedicated pool.
- No API-level 5xx surge observed, but increased client perceived latency causing support complaints.

Environment:
- Dedicated capacity (customer-owned pool) in ap-southeast-1 region, nodes backed by multizone GPU hosts.
- API nodes fronted by global edge routing and smart-routing policies that can route to us-west-2 fallback when local capacity is constrained.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Send authenticated chat generation request pinned to NimbleHealth dedicated model rw-instruct-7b-v2 from a client in Singapore.
2) Observe TTFB via curl -w '%{time_starttransfer}
'.
3) Repeat 1000 requests over 10m window; elevated TTFB observed on ~12–18% of requests.

Observed signals and logs:
- Grafana trace gaps show initial connection and TLS handshake times normal; delay occurs after routing decision and before first token generation (time between router->serving-runtime connection and first token).
- Edge logs show a subset of requests were routed to us-west-2 despite origin being ap-southeast-1.
- BGP peering/aggr metrics show transient asymmetric egress on one of the ap-southeast-1 egress routers during the incident window.
- No quota/429s; no scale-up events triggered for dedicated pool during window.
investigation_notes:
03/10 09:12 - Initial triage by Support (Maya): customer-provided traces and curl timings indicate TTFB spikes.
03/10 10:05 - Eng oncall (Luis) pulled edge routing logs; saw ~15% sessions routed to us-west-2 via fallback policy.
03/10 11:30 - Network team ran BGP/peering checks: found flapping on ap-southeast-1 egress-router-2 causing some sessions to take a longer as-path to upstream peer.
03/10 12:20 - Hypothesis: transient egress path asymmetry caused the smart-routing decision to prefer fallback region for a subset of requests, adding inter-region latency. Corroborated by flow logs showing routing hops crossing to us-west-2.
03/11 02:45 - Verified dedicated pool capacity normal; no autoscale anomalies.
03/11 08:10 - Replayed traffic from a synthetic agent in SG and observed occasional reroutes when egress-router-2 reported high prepkt-loss.
03/12 14:00 - Network vendor applied control-plane fix for egress-router-2; flapping cleared.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:25 - Maya Chen (Support): Customer reports chat UX slowness. Asked for sample request IDs and cURL TTFB output. Customer provided 6 request IDs and timestamps.
2026-03-10 10:12 - Luis Ortega (SRE): Confirmed some requests were served from us-west-2. Opening INT-2103 for network investigation and tagging networking team.
2026-03-10 11:40 - Anika Patel (Network Eng): Observed BGP session resets on ap-southeast-1 egress-router-2 between 08:40-09:20 UTC; suspect upstream peer instability.
2026-03-11 09:18 - Maya Chen (Support): Customer notes that issue frequency reduced after 03/10 16:00 UTC but still sees occasional spikes (~5%). Asked for ETA to fully resolve.

2026-03-12 14:05 - Luis Ortega (SRE): Network vendor applied fix; flapping cleared. Monitoring for 24h to confirm stable routing. Notified customer and recommended temporary routing constraints to pin to local egress until stable.

2026-03-12 15:10 - Customer (NimbleHealth - Alex Rivera): Acknowledged reduction in spikes; requested confirmation that no config change required on their side and asked for postmortem when incident closed.
resolution:
Mitigation applied: constrained smart-routing policy for NimbleHealth to prefer ap-southeast-1 egress until network flapping fully resolved (temporary routing override). Network vendor fixed BGP peer causing egress-router-2 flapping.

Root cause: transient instability on a regional egress router (ap-southeast-1) caused asymmetric/longer egress paths; smart-routing fallback logic routed a minority of sessions to us-west-2 which added ~600–1200ms TTFB.

Workaround: Applied customer-scoped routing bias to prefer local egress and avoid fallback for short windows; advised customer to retry transient failures with backoff.

Follow-ups:
- INT-2103: Improve telemetry so routing decision logs include egress-router health markers (owner: Networking, ETA: 2026-03-25).
- Add a canary for BGP session metrics in ap-southeast-1 to detect flapping earlier (owner: Observability, ETA: 2026-03-20).
- Postmortem to be published to Confluence and shared with NimbleHealth (owner: Support/Ops, target: 2026-03-18).
next_steps:
1) Keep temporary routing override in place for 48h of stable telemetry.
2) Network team to complete two follow-up tasks (telemetry & canary).
3) Draft postmortem and share with customer, include recommended platform changes to surface egress health in routing decisions.
4) Re-evaluate smart-routing fallback thresholds to avoid cross-region routing for short-lived egress instabilities.
